messages:
raj.khan: Heads-up — audit asked for a 7-year retention window on auth and admin logs for a customer compliance review. Current SIEM export only holds 1 year. Can we discuss options?
ana-g: yikes. is this for hosted or Private?
matt-b: which indices exactly? auth events, admin DDL, KMS key ops?
raj.khan: primarily auth (login/fail), admin console actions, and KMS key usage. It's for a regulated customer on Dedicated but asking company-wide baseline.
lisa_ops: we have two knobs: increase long-term S3 export retention (cheap) or push into our cold archive with lifecycle rules + indexed metadata in SIEM for searchability. Both have tradeoffs on queryability and cost.
nana-g: note we must ensure KMS-wrapped objects remain decryptable for the retention period. If we rotate customer keys, we need key escrow or rewrap plan.
matt-b: good call. For Dedicated customers we currently have key-rotation policy that rotates every 90 days. No escrow.
sec-bot: incident-note: previous key rotation caused inability to decrypt 2023 logs for one customer — resolved by restore from pre-rotation backup.
raj.khan: so options: 1) extend SIEM export retention to 7y (S3 + Athena partitioning) and maintain key policies to retain old key versions; 2) export raw logs to GCS/S3 cold with separate KMS-managed encryption key and escrow; 3) keep 1y hot in SIEM and plumb a searchable index with pointers to cold objects. Which is least operationally risky?
lisa_ops: #1 simplest for search but expensive. #2 safest for encryption isolation but we need an escrow and replay tooling. #3 lowest cost but adds friction when auditors ask for quick queries.
matt-b: also RBAC: who gets access to long-term buckets? We need stricter ACLs + audit logging on accesses. Right now ops has broad read on backup buckets.
nana-g: agree. For compliance we should create a dedicated role (security-log-archive-reader) and gate via IAM + just-in-time access for audits. Add an approval workflow in Vault and require an ADR log entry.
raj.khan: can we do time-limited KMS grants? e.g., use envelope keys that we can revoke after a TTL so auditors get temporary access rather than permanent bucket read perms.
matt-b: AWS KMS has grants with constraints, but for S3 encryption we often rely on object-level CMK access. We could adopt envelope encryption with a separate archive CMK and rotate it only with manual escrow. That lets us revoke quickly.
lisa_ops: I'll draft an operational runbook: storage path, retention lifecycle (7y), who can request access, audit steps, and the KMS escrow process. Assigning to @lisa_ops to start.
nana-g: also add a migration plan: reingest critical indices into a read-only SIEM index for the last 7y so queries are fast for compliance searches. Could run a nightly job to index metadata for cold objects.
sec-bot: deploy-bot: created ticket SEC-8943 — "7y retention for security logs: design + RBAC + KMS escrow" assigned to lisa_ops.
raj.khan: thanks. follow-ups: lisa, can you propose cost estimate and an emergency access playbook by EOD Friday? I'll coordinate with legal on the auditor's exact data scope.
lisa_ops: on it. rough estimate by tomorrow morning, full doc by Friday EOD.
matt-b: will review RBAC changes. tagging infra to audit current bucket ACLs and list principals.
nana-g: and I'll review KMS policies and draft example grant commands. snippet for grant:```
aws kms create-grant --key-id arn:aws:kms:... --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/security-log-archive-reader --operations Encrypt Decrypt GenerateDataKey --constraints EncryptedDataPackage=...```
raj.khan: perfect. keep thread slim — post updates here. :thumbsup:
